about: Parity contract cases. designc owns renderer/parity.js; any recorder or pipeline that compares UI for designc runs these too. shape: Parity.shape on each value and Parity.sameShape on the pair. diff: Parity.normalise each side (masks from the case, expect from the side), Parity.exceptions(case.exceptions), Parity.diff; the findings, as kind and severity, must equal the list.

diff.about: A date column in another format is one shape failure.
Other values in the same format pass: data is not compared.
A renamed column header is one text failure.
The same rename is covered by an acceptance criterion locator naming the new header.
Lost thousands separators are a shape failure.
Sorting by a column gives the opposite order on the new app.
Different values ordered by the same rule pass.
A filter that leaves a row that does not match fails on the new app.
Two Edit buttons against one: the second is missing.
The missing button is covered by a bound business decision that removes it.
The same buttons in another order are one order failure.
A button legacy does not have is an extra failure.
A button inside a grid cell is interface text.
A link carrying the cell text is the record's data, not interface text.
A status in another case class is a shape failure.
A vocabulary column masked exact is compared word for word.
A button disabled in legacy and enabled in the new app.
A button 6 px taller at the same viewport fails; 2 px does not.
Boxes are not compared when the viewports differ.
A count or a time in a message is not a wording change.
A field showing a date in another format is a shape failure.
